feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: International news, global reporting and analysis from NPR. Plus dispatches from NPR’s State of the World podcast.

entry.title: Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
entry.summary: Senegal's breakdancers have been practicing for their country's historic hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month. It's the first time Africa is hosting an Olympic event.

entry.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a prisoner exchange as talks end with no big breakthrough
entry.summary: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi led to this decision, marking the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022.

entry.title: House effectively ends Hegseth impeachment. And, 3 men accused of plotting U.K. attacks
entry.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has been spared from the House's impeachment effort, at least for now. And, federal prosecutors arrested three men accused of being Iran-backed operatives.

entry.title: An Iran-backed trio is accused of plotting attacks on a U.K. base hosting U.S. jets
entry.summary: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.

entry.title: Spain's workers hold a general strike over housing costs before national election
entry.summary: Millions of Spanish workers have shut down businesses and disrupted transportation in a protest over housing costs. The strike on Wednesday was the first general strike in Spain in 14 years, culminating in huge marches of tens of thousands of workers and average citizens in downtown Barcelona and Madrid, along with gatherings in other cities.

entry.title: Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak
entry.summary: Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease.

entry.title: U.S. boycotts U.N. human rights review for second year running
entry.summary: The U.S. has skipped a key U.N. human rights review for the second year running. Rights groups warn the absence risks undermining global accountability.

entry.title: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
entry.summary: Little is known about her except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, but Korea's spy agency says she's likely her father's heir.

entry.title: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility
entry.summary: His resignation offer comes amid a widening political rift between Prabowo and Widodo and a separate investigation into allegations that senior police officials wiretapped the president.

entry.title: House set to vote to impeach Hegseth. And, SCOTUS allows border wall work to proceed
entry.summary: The House could vote to impeach Hegseth, but removing him from office will be tough. And, SCOTUS ruled that a federal judge did not have the authority to halt border wall construction.
